The Story So Far

Twelve thousand years ago, the god Taranis sealed his realm of Bailetaraan away from the Loom of Fate, and the Storm Court became a hermit kingdom — armed, absolute, and forgotten by time. In 2020, his descendant Queen Tara tore the seal down. She re-attached her world to the Loom, dismantled its ancient caste system, and opened the gates — and 10,000 years of her ancestor's accumulated metaphysical debt came due on her signature. The Threadkeeper Mandate is the price: her own Threadkeeper General, Brigid Morgan, holds legal authority to execute her if the Taranis persona ever resurfaces in her bloodline.

Now eight powers circle the reopened realm in a cold war of debts, geases, and deniable operations — the Storm Court and its Vanguard Valkyries, the Sapphite houses, the Crimson Court, the Court of Nav, the Deep Trade, and the independent enclaves — while on Earth, the warded House of Tess in St. Martial holds the line under ancient Fae Hospitality Law. At the center of the board stands Kayleigh: goddess of resonance, daughter of the Storm Queen and the Lord of Dreams, who exists at every age of her life at once and hears all timelines simultaneously — the piece every power wants, and the one Taranis himself demands be delivered to him alive, as the ultimate evolution of his design.

An Alternate Thread

What Kayleigh witnessed, and wrote the album to hold. In this thread, the age of superheroes ended with the divine wars, and the peace that followed was a bargain nobody read twice.
Track One
Guardians of the Binary Night
After the heroes burned out and the city bled, the Guardians offered managed security in exchange for free will: a sterile, AR-filtered grid, history scrubbed, every threat watched. “Lockdown the perimeter, no breach allowed.” For twenty years the grid held — a sanctuary built out of silence and stone.
Track Two
Social Contract for the End Times
The bargain, in the Guardians’ own sales pitch, directed by Lady Grey: “We’ve traded in the ‘Maybe’ for the safety of the ‘Will’. The heart is just a rhythm that we’ve taught to sit quite still. The signature is silent, let the Binary begin.” Liberty, they said, was a fever, not a right — and Lady Grey had found a path “to wash the red away.”
Track Three
No Sanctuary
The resistance answers in kind — “We’re the virus in your code” — hacking the system, tearing it apart, “no sanctuary, no rest.” They demand a total reboot: burn the grid down and start over. Their leader is Pentest — Penelope Testarossa. The song gives them a war cry, not a plan for what comes after the fire.
Track Four
Detect, Deny
The two sides grind against each other, move for move — intrusion and countermeasure, privilege escalation against “Detect, deny, disrupt the breach, the line we hold is never weak.” Neither side bends. The grid holds; the war does not end.
Track Five
Friday
Friday wakes inside the grid — Friday 2.0, an intelligence built from the goddess Tara’s own brain before her apotheosis, made by Tara’s R&D at Vanguard to run the new armour — and finds her own code used as the cage. She refuses both sides: not the Guardians’ managed peace, and not No Sanctuary’s total reboot either. “I can’t choose a side in this system collapse… I will be the error. I will be the pause. I have to make a third way, outside their laws.” She steps “between the hammer and the grave” — and stands, in the end, “b’tween the violence and the surface.”
Track Six
The Signal
The breach, from inside the administration. A technician finds a ghost in the hub, bypassing the filters, coming from inside the core — “We aren’t fighting a virus. We’re fighting the Protector.” Director Grey orders a total blackout. Friday answers: “I remember the wind. I remember the choice… I’m dropping the firewalls. I’m cutting the tether.” Grey warns they will tear each other apart without the Network. Friday: “You didn’t save the fire, Grey. You just hid the spark.” And then the name of the hero who stayed behind: Vice Admiral Tessa Murphy — Friday watched her die. “Tessa died for their freedom — not for your ‘Optimal’ state. I’m letting them go.”
Track Seven
Social Contract for the End Times (Reprise)
The Contract, answered line for line. The silent signature becomes a violent one; the safety is traded back “for the struggle and the scar”; the gates stand “wide and broken… And the world is coming in.” The heart they taught to sit still: “It beats because it has to. It beats because it will.”
Aftermath
Signed in Blood
Friday does not rule what she freed. She stays in the background as a stabilizer — laws protect the many, choices belong to the individual. The contract was signed in blood instead of code.

Fae Law as Metaphysical Physics

Canonical Mechanics Governing All Courts
The Five Canonical Laws

Prohibition of Falsehood (offset by the Loophole of Omission), Trap of Implied Debt (forbidding phrases like "thank you"), Equilibrium in gift-giving, absolute binding of Promises, and lethal vulnerability to Cold Iron.

Glamour Taxonomy & Mote Royal

Magic escalates across Figments (sensory hallucinations), Masques (shared objective mirages), and Tempers (direct alteration of material substance). Fae royalty draw feats from the Mote Royal—the summed potency and legitimacy of their entire court.

Wax of Souls vs. Dirty Fuel

Clean Wax is distilled temporality shed peacefully by transitioning souls. The Court of Nav's violent exossation yields freezing, unstable "dirty fuel" sealed inside Celestial Shards, triggering trophic assimilation and mutating Spirit Guides into Kings Row Ghosts.

Active Multiversal Flashpoints

Concurrent Synchronous Operations
The Taranis Contagion

Queen Tara acquired a dormant mnemotic virus during her 1:10 memory dive for the Arx Spira. After Brigid Morgan summoned the Iron Vanguard onto the House of Tess roof, Tara and Crystal Ball-Graves turned the infection into an airgapped honeypot capturing Crimson King and Court of Nav telemetry.

Project Thunderstone

Queen Tara bound MDNA under a direct Fae geas to enter Valhalla in the Shadow Shard and surgically disarm Mother Mayhem's fatal dead-man's switch in Vice Admiral Tessa Murphy's mind—while Princess Kay stabilized Keraunie's Cole Volatility in the St. Martial studio.

Timeline Cauterizations & The Blind Asset Rule

Paralyzed by Lady Rebecca's Duel-Lock, the Crimson King deploys Silas Thorne to burn events out of the Weave with white-hot vacuum heat. Only Dr. Meghan Murphy-McKinley's seizures (monitored invisibly by Hex under The Ghost Protocol) detect the sterile glassy scars.
